extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, scientists, and scholars interested in method and reforming the sciences (early‑modern/Foundational context)
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidelines for rebuilding natural philosophy: how to collect and arrange experiment, form axioms, avoid past errors, and organize inquiry for the advancement of the sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reward and encouragement for scientific endeavour
rubrics_metrics.description: The advancement of science is repressed when attempts and industry pass unrewarded; cultivation and reward belong to different individuals and lack of popular praise discourages progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that scientific attempts are recognized and rewarded; without reward and popular praise, excellent work is likely to be neglected or extinguished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combat despair and cultivate reasonable hope
rubrics_metrics.description: Men’s despair and the idea of impossibility are great obstacles; prudent minds are diffident due to obscurity of nature, shortness of life, deception of senses, and weakness of judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare minds by exposing grounds for reasonable hope (examples, analogies, and tables of invention) to encourage industry and experiment rather than producing gloom; provide cogent means and particulars that support hope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose and correct past errors to enable progress
rubrics_metrics.description: If past failures are due to human error rather than the nature of things, then by banishing or correcting these errors a great change for the better can be produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically identify and expose mistakes of prior methods and practice so that future work can avoid the same pitfalls and build on corrected foundations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine experiment and reason (the bee metaphor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither pure empiricism (heap up facts like ants) nor pure dogmatism (spin webs like spiders) suffices; the true labour of philosophy is like the bee: it extracts matter from observation and works it in the understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate experimental collection with rational processing — gather facts and actively work them into understanding rather than merely storing them or merely speculating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue a pure, unmixed natural philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural philosophy is now impure and corrupted by Aristotelian logic, Platonic theology, and inappropriate mathematics; better results are expected from a pure and unmixed natural philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid allowing external systems of thought (that are not methodologies for natural inquiry) to dominate natural philosophy; aim for a discipline focused on interpreting nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin inquiry with an unprejudiced, clear mind
rubrics_metrics.description: No one has yet shown sufficient firmness to abolish common theories and apply the mind afresh; a person of mature age, unprejudiced senses, and clear mind starting anew promises great advancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage investigators to clear preconceived opinions and start from particulars and direct experience when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compile a robust natural history as the foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations of experience have been weak; a store and collection of particular facts capable of informing the mind has not been sufficiently sought or amassed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect comprehensive natural history intended specifically as the raw material for philosophical interpretation (not merely descriptive catalogs). Distinguish histories compiled for their own sake from histories gathered to inform theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect 'enlightening' experiments (not only profitable ones)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanical experiments useful to a craftsman are often uninformative for causes; we require experiments that assist materially in the discovery of causes and axioms — 'enlightening' experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize experiments whose outcomes decisively inform causal questions (they 'never deceive or fail you') even if they are of no direct practical use; distinguish these from experiments done only for profit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a regular method, order, and progression of experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Vague and arbitrary experience is mere groping in the dark; experience must proceed regularly and uninterruptedly by a determined rule for sciences to advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and follow clear procedures and rules for observation and experimentation rather than relying on haphazard or occasional findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record observations in writing rather than rely on memory
rubrics_metrics.description: Meditation has hitherto done more for discovery than writing because experiments have not been committed to paper; the understanding cannot act on materials by memory alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit experiments and observations to written records to enable reliable accumulation, transmission, and analysis of data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize particulars into well-arranged 'tables of discovery'
rubrics_metrics.description: A multitude of particulars lying widely dispersed distracts the understanding; order them by means of proper and well-arranged living tables of discovery which the mind can apply to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create systematic tables (catalogues, indices, matrices) that present particulars in an organized form to facilitate comparison, exclusion, and induction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use particulars to ascend to axioms and descend to effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rest at the discovery of new particulars; more important results come from deducing axioms from particulars and then using axioms to predict or define new particulars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat research as a cycle: collect particulars, derive intermediate axioms, then apply those axioms to discover new effects and particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid leaping from particulars to remote general axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: The understanding must not jump from particulars to the most general abstract axioms; assent should proceed by a true scale and successive steps from particulars to lesser axioms and upward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build knowledge in successive, intermediate steps (particulars → lesser axioms → intermediate axioms → general axioms) rather than inferring overly-general principles prematurely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invent and use a rigorous form of induction (method of exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Induction by simple enumeration is puerile and unsafe; a useful induction should separate nature by proper rejections and exclusions and then affirm after collecting sufficient negatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop an inductive procedure that identifies and eliminates alternative causes (using negative instances) before concluding affirmative generalizations — go beyond mere enumeration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate axioms by their ability to predict new particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: In forming axioms, examine whether they are only fitted to the instances from which they are deduced or whether they are truly more extensive; observe whether they confirm their extent by pointing out new particulars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test proposed axioms by their generative power: an axiom's credibility increases if it reliably indicates new, previously unobserved particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate sciences to prevent dismembering of knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Extend natural philosophy and reduce particular sciences to that one so as to prevent schism or dismembering of the sciences; integration is necessary to advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor frameworks that connect particular inquiries under common methods and principles rather than allowing irreconcilable fragmentation between disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematize transfer and comparison of knowledge across arts (literate experience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many inventions have been discovered by chance; better results may be obtained by transferring, comparing, and applying known operations across arts by literate experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage cross-domain comparison and the deliberate transfer of methods and experiments from one art to another to generate new inventions and insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be attentive to simple systemic improvements (look for overlooked obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some inventions (e.g., printing) remained unknown for ages due to neglect of simple but systemic advantages; the mind often misses obvious improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively seek simple structural or procedural changes that may have outsized effects (e.g., changes in organization, materials, or orientation) rather than assuming novelty must be complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate sufficient talent, time, and resources for compiling natural history
rubrics_metrics.description: A collection of natural and experimental history is a great and royal work requiring much labour and expense; much talent, time, and fortune are squandered on inferior studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit adequate resources and organized labor to the large project of gathering and curating natural history rather than dispersing effort on trivial pursuits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace the multitude of particulars as an advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not be alarmed at the multitude of particulars; particulars are relatively few compared to imaginative fictions, and thorough examination leads to termination of method while speculation is infinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persist in collecting and organizing particulars; the profusion of facts is a surmountable and productive condition, not a reason to despair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor division of labor and cooperative accumulation of data
rubrics_metrics.description: One who has progressed somewhat suggests what may be hoped from those who enjoy abundant leisure, united labours, and the succession of ages — each performing separate parts accelerates progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize collaborative networks where investigators share duties (e.g., each collects and records different portions of natural history) to build the corpus more rapidly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attempt experiments despite risk of failure (better small loss than neglect)
rubrics_metrics.description: The risk attending want of success is not to be compared with that of neglecting the attempt; the former costs little labour, the latter an immense benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage experimental attempts even when success is uncertain; the potential cost of inaction outweighs the small loss from failed trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not found sects or promise particular effects; aim to derive causes and axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: The intention is not to found philosophical sects nor to promise particular effects; rather the method is to deduce causes and axioms from experiments, and new effects from those axioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid speculative systems and partisan schools of thought; focus on building a methodology that derives lawful causes from observation which can then generate effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept early errors in natural history but ensure they are correctable
rubrics_metrics.description: Early collections will contain mistakes; small errors (like a misprinted letter) are not a great inconvenience and can be expunged when causes and axioms are discovered, but frequent serious errors undermine the enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow for and expect corrigible errors in early stages, but design scrutiny and mechanisms to detect and correct persistent or systematic errors in the corpus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include common, mean, and even sordid particulars in inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Common and mean particulars are often neglected but their causes are essential for understanding rarer phenomena; the mean and splendid alike exist and deserve study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not exclude ordinary, lowly, or 'filthy' phenomena from natural history; detailed study of common things can yield fundamental causal knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value 'light' (knowledge) over immediate profit; include speculative 'useless' inquiries for illumination
rubrics_metrics.description: Some matters may appear refined and useless, but knowledge of simple natures affords 'light' and leads to powerful axioms and numerous effects later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize experiments and records that increase understanding ('light') even if they have no immediate material utility; these seeds can generate later practical benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postpone scholastic subtle disputes until after axioms are discovered
rubrics_metrics.description: Subtile disputes and discursive efforts are late and preposterous when introduced before discovery of axioms; their chief opportunity is when experiment is to be weighed and axioms derived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay abstruse theoretical disputation until an empirical foundation and axioms have been established; allow experimentation and induction to precede fine metaphysical debate.
